name: Innocuous Ox (Shor Tam) — Liability from Body of Ox
notes: The principle that an innocuous ox's owner pays only half-damages exclusively from proceeds of the sale of the belligerent ox, not from other assets

name: Tooth and Foot Damage (Shen veTefes/Regel)
notes: Detailed rules for the primary categories of Tooth (eating) and Foot (trampling) damage, including exemption in public domain and payment for benefit derived

name: Pit Depth Requirement for Liability
notes: Rule that a pit must be at least ten handbreadths deep to create full liability for death; lesser depth creates liability only for injury

name: Pit Liability — Exemption for Vessels
notes: Torah edict exempting the digger of a pit from liability for damage to vessels (as opposed to animals) that fall in

name: Person Always Forewarned (Adam Muad leOlam)
notes: The principle that a person is always considered forewarned for damage he causes, whether intentional or unintentional, asleep or awake, requiring full damages

name: Fire Damage — Liability for Spread of Fire
notes: Detailed rules on how far fire can spread before owner loses liability, including disputes of Rabbi Eliezer, Rabbi Akiva, and Rabbi Shimon

name: Fire Damage — Hidden Items in Stack
notes: Dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbis whether one who sets fire to a stack is liable for concealed vessels inside it; in a house, all agree he is liable

name: Robbery with Change (Shinui) — Acquisition by Transformation
notes: A robber who transforms stolen property (e.g., wood into vessels, wool into garments) acquires it via the change, and pays value at time of robbery rather than returning the item

name: Robbery Valuation at Time of Theft
notes: Principle that robbers pay according to the value of the stolen item at the time of the robbery, even if it subsequently appreciated or depreciated

name: Robbery with False Oath — Additional Fifth (Chomesh)
notes: One who robs and takes a false oath must pay principal plus one-fifth additional, and bring a guilt offering; the one-fifth compounds if he takes further false oaths

name: Robbing a Convert Who Died Without Heirs — Payment to Priests
notes: One who robs a convert who subsequently dies without heirs must pay the principal plus a fifth to the priests and bring a guilt-offering

name: Owner's Despair of Recovery (Yiush)
notes: When an owner despairs of recovering stolen or lost property, another person may acquire the item; relevant to salvage from river, troop, bandits, and swarms

name: Returning Robbery in Settled vs. Unsettled Area
notes: One who robbed in a settled area may not return the item in an unsettled area where it is of no benefit to the owner

name: Liability for Objects Left in Public Domain
notes: Rules on liability for damage caused by objects left or spilled in public domain, including thorns, water, straw, hay, and poured liquids

name: Damage Between Two People Walking in Public Domain
notes: Rules for when two people or carriers collide in public domain — including barrel vs. cross beam, walking vs. running — determining liability based on direction and stopping

name: Five Payments for Bodily Injury
notes: The five components of compensation for bodily injury: damage (nezek), pain (tza'ar), medical costs (ripui), loss of livelihood (shevet), and humiliation (boshet)

name: Pain Compensation (Tza'ar)
notes: Compensation for pain caused by injury, assessed by how much the victim would accept to undergo such pain; separate from damage to the body's monetary value

name: Medical Cost Compensation (Ripui)
notes: Ongoing obligation to pay for the injured party's medical treatment; if wound reopens, liability continues; ends when wound fully heals

name: Loss of Livelihood Compensation (Shevet)
notes: Compensation for income lost during convalescence, assessed as wages of a cucumber watchman (not the victim's professional wages, which are subsumed in the damage payment)

name: Humiliation Assessment (Boshet) — Factors and Method
notes: Method and factors for assessing humiliation damages, including the dignity of both parties; specific fixed amounts for slap, back-of-hand slap, spitting, uncovering a woman's head

name: Capital Liability Exempts from Monetary Payment
notes: One who is liable for capital punishment for an act (e.g., injuring a parent, desecrating Shabbat) is exempt from monetary payments for the same act

name: Double Payment for Theft (Kefel) — Detailed Rules
notes: Detailed rules on when kefel applies: admission vs. witness testimony, stolen-then-stolen items, partial sales, invalid slaughter, and interaction with fourfold/fivefold payments

name: Fourfold and Fivefold Payment (Arba v'Chamisha)
notes: Fourfold payment for sheep and fivefold for ox when a thief slaughters or sells a stolen animal; detailed rules on when this applies vs. only double payment

name: Prohibition on Purchasing from Suspected Thieves
notes: Prohibition on purchasing wool, milk, kids, wood, or produce from shepherds and watchmen who tend others' property, due to presumption of theft

name: Craftsman's Payment — Enhancement vs. Expenses
notes: When a craftsman performs work improperly or damages, the owner pays only the lesser of enhancement or expenses; dispute regarding dyer who dyed wrong color

name: Craftsman Who Damages the Work
notes: Craftsmen (carpenter, builder, dyer) who damage items entrusted to them are liable to pay for the damage caused

name: Ox Goring a Slave — Thirty Shekel Payment
notes: Fixed payment of thirty sela when an ox kills a Canaanite slave, regardless of the slave's actual value (whether worth one dinar or one hundred maneh)

name: Ransom Payment (Kofer) for Forewarned Ox that Kills
notes: Owner of a forewarned ox that kills a person pays ransom (kofer); owner of innocuous ox is exempt from ransom; both oxen are put to death

name: Prohibition on Raising Small Animals in Settled Eretz Yisrael
hebrew: איסור גידול בהמה דקה ביישוב ארץ ישראל
notes: Rabbinic prohibition on raising small livestock (sheep, goats) in settled areas of Eretz Yisrael due to crop damage; permitted in Syria and wilderness

name: Regional Disaster Exemption for Robber (Massikin)
notes: If thugs seize a robbed field as part of a regional seizure, the robber is exempt (the field would have been taken anyway); if they came specifically due to the robber, he must compensate

name: Salvage and Compensation — Rescuing Another's Property
notes: One who salvages another's property (honey, donkey) without agreement is entitled only to wage compensation; prior agreement obligates owner to pay the full value of what the rescuer sacrificed

name: Craftsman's Claim to Remnants and Threads
notes: Rules on which scraps, threads, and shavings belong to the craftsman (launderer, carder, tailor, carpenter) vs. the customer, based on whether the customer values them

name: Ox Forewarned for One Species/Type but Not Another
notes: An ox may be forewarned regarding one species, size category, or day (e.g., Shabbat) but innocuous for others, with differential liability accordingly

name: Goring by Ownerless, Consecrated, or Gentile Ox — Exemptions
hebrew: נגיחת שור הפקר והקדש ושל גוי
notes: Exemptions from ox-goring liability when the goring or gored ox is consecrated property; and the rule that a gentile's ox that gores a Jew's ox is always liable for full damages

name: Transfer of Ox to Bailee — Shifting Responsibility
notes: When an owner conveys a dangerous ox to a bailee (unpaid, borrower, paid, renter), the bailee assumes the owner's liability for damage caused by the ox

name: Pigeon Trap Distance Rule
notes: Prohibition on spreading traps for pigeons within thirty ris of any settled area to prevent catching privately owned birds

name: Requesting Forgiveness After Paying Damages
notes: Even after paying all monetary compensation, an assailant must request forgiveness from the victim; without forgiveness the transgression is not fully atoned

name: Self-Injury: Exempt for Self, Liable for Others
notes: One who injures himself is exempt from penalties, but others who cause the same injury are liable; analogously, one who damages his own property is exempt but others are liable

name: Konam Vow Affecting Inheritance
notes: If a father vowed that his son may not benefit from his property, the son may inherit after father's death (no longer the father's property), unless the vow explicitly covered life and death

name: Compensation for Miscarriage (Nezek Vlad)
notes: A person who causes a woman to miscarry must pay compensation for the miscarried offspring to the husband; assessed by value difference of the woman before and after birth, or by value of offspring
